title: Composition with Large Blue Plane, Red, Black, Yellow, and Gray
lede: A 1921 Mondrian in which one bright blue plane takes the upper right, balanced by a small red strip, a black block, and a yellow square at the opposite edges.
summary: A large blue plane at upper right against gray and white, with red, black, and yellow at the edges. Piet Mondrian, 1921.

source.label: Dallas Museum of Art: Composition with Large Blue Plane, Red, Black, Yellow, and Gray

evidence.note: Inspected the Dallas Museum of Art photograph on [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Piet_Mondrian_-_Composition_with_Large_Blue_Plane,_Red,_Black,_Yellow,_and_Gray_-_1984.200.FA_-_Dallas_Museum_of_Art.jpg) (7028 × 8465 px, viewed at 960 px), object 1984.200.FA. The photograph includes the white frame edge and a color checker strip at the top, which the stored copy crops off. Catalogue facts are from the museum’s record on Google Arts & Culture.

styles.note: A textbook neoplastic composition: one dominant primary plane, small opposing color planes at the far edges, gray and white fields, and black lines that stop short of some edges.

context: Oil on canvas, 60.33 × 49.85 cm. Dallas Museum of Art, Foundation for the Arts Collection, gift of Mrs. James H. Clark, 1984.200.FA. [Google Arts & Culture](https://artsandculture.google.com/asset/composition-with-large-blue-plane-red-black-yellow-and-gray/CwE7U9R78Q2UOQ).

The museum’s text quotes Mondrian: “Color exists only through another color, dimension is defined by another dimension.” [Google Arts & Culture](https://artsandculture.google.com/asset/composition-with-large-blue-plane-red-black-yellow-and-gray/CwE7U9R78Q2UOQ).
observed: A bright blue plane covers the upper right, about a third of the canvas; a black line divides its lower part into two smaller blue cells.
A narrow orange-red strip runs down part of the left edge beside a black rectangle.
A small pale yellow square sits at the bottom right, below a white cell.
The rest of the surface is light gray and white; the grays differ slightly from plane to plane.
The black lines are thick and even. The top-left line stops before the left edge, and the lowest vertical line stops above the bottom edge.
interpretation: The painting shows the rubric’s balance by opposition in its clearest form: the one large color plane is answered by three small ones in the far corners.
Lines that stop short of the edge keep the grid from reading as a closed table, which is a detail most web imitations miss.
borrow: Give one primary most of the color area and use the other two only as small accents in the opposite corners.
End some divider lines a little before the container edge.

images.alt: Abstract painting: a large bright blue plane at upper right, divided by black lines, light gray and white planes at left and below, a narrow red strip and a black block at the lower left edge, and a small yellow square at the bottom right.
images.caption: Piet Mondrian, Composition with Large Blue Plane, Red, Black, Yellow, and Gray, 1921. Dallas Museum of Art, 1984.200.FA. Photograph from [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Piet_Mondrian_-_Composition_with_Large_Blue_Plane,_Red,_Black,_Yellow,_and_Gray_-_1984.200.FA_-_Dallas_Museum_of_Art.jpg), public domain; the color checker strip is cropped off.

rights.statement: Commons marks the museum photograph PD-Art with PD-old-auto-expired: Mondrian died in 1944, so the work is public domain in the Netherlands since 2015. Painted in 1921, it is public domain in the United States as a work published before 1931, and also under the life-plus-70 rule if it counts as unpublished.
